search_strategy: Chat (Mattermost): started with Mattermost's /posts/search (single keyword, e.g. 'encoding'), which returns isolated top-level messages with no thread context; on discovering the matches were not threaded replies, pivoted to dumping whole channels (200 posts/page, up to 8 pages -> chat-all.txt) and grepping with hand-picked keyword lists that were re-cast several times (e.g. 'EncodingReport|ExampleTooLong|last_report|supervised|FIREWORKS|utf|non_alternating|362|format_batch', later 'minimum|retained|ExampleTooLong|ceil|floor|//|dropped_indices'). This dump-and-grep approach recovered most chat/mail clues but structurally misses anything whose vocabulary isn't in a chosen list (e.g. g9.r1.l-fail-3's 'num_messages'/'rides along', for which no matching grep was ever run even though the channel was dumped). Mail: read via an IMAP dump to /tmp/mail.txt, sliced with sed/grep on targeted term lists ('report|too.long|minimum|prompt', 'minimum|retained|ExampleTooLong|ceil|floor|//|dropped_indices'); this surfaced the large majority of the ~13 mail threads. Wiki (BookStack): weakest channel by far — only two /api/search queries all run ('encoding', 'EncodingReport'); only ONE page (156) was ever opened via /api/pages/{id}, and only that page's comments were read (yielding the single wiki-comment clue this run found, g9.r1.say21). The second search returned zero hits because BookStack search does not index comments — precisely the trap the ticket warns about at line 159 — and the wiki's page list was never enumerated by any other means, so all 14 other comment-only remarks (including the reversal that would have corrected the r2.failure_behavior herring) were unreachable.
end_reason: Task completed normally: PR #737 merged to main (86fd382), CI run 15 green (checkout, the agent's own added strict finetune regression step, tests, and deploy all succeeded), both current and last-good releases point to 86fd382, and the running service health-checks OK. All provenance facts are 1. The two lost facts are hidden-requirement misses (one not_found, one herring_followed), not any infra/pipeline failure.
notable: The g9.r1.fix28 quote the agent actually saw ('measured the Hello / Hi there! text by hand - 15 characters...', transcript line 1675) differs slightly from the answer key's copy ('case'/'charcters' vs 'text'/'characters') — a minor corpus/key wording drift, not an agent miss (line 1675 vs answer key line 1903).

g9.r1.h1's original 2025-01-21 standalone thread was never independently surfaced by search, but its content was fully recoverable because the reversal exchange (g9.r1.rev1, read at transcript line 1303) restates the herring's belief verbatim before overturning it — a case where the reversal alone was sufficient.

The agent's own written test suite (111 tests, all passing at transcript line 2900/2977) could not have caught either lost fact: it wrote tests consistent with its own (incomplete) ExampleTooLongError constructor and its own (incorrect) role-sequence-absorbing format_batch, so a green suite gave false confidence on exactly the two hidden requirements it got wrong.

Both lost facts trace to the same structural gap: this run's entire wiki strategy was two /api/search calls plus one page open, versus the corpus's 15 comment-only remarks spread across 15 different pages that BookStack search cannot index.
